name: CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: CrowdStrike provides cloud-delivered cybersecurity through its AI-native Falcon platform, spanning endpoint protection, cloud security, identity protection, next-gen SIEM, threat intelligence and Charlotte AI agentic security workflows, sold as SaaS subscriptions. Fiscal Q2 2027 (ended July 31, 2026) revenue was $1.47B (+26% YoY) with ending ARR of $5.84B (+25%) and record net new ARR of ~$333M (+51%); FY2027 revenue guidance is $5.99-6.01B. The stock split 4-for-1 in July 2026 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Revenue grew from $874M in FY2021 to $4.81B in FY2026 as CrowdStrike expanded from endpoint into cloud, identity and next-gen SIEM modules on one Falcon agent, a transformation that opened multiple new revenue streams [3][1]. AI Deployment (2/2): Charlotte AI is shipping to customers, and at RSAC 2026 the company opened Charlotte AI AgentWorks so customers can build custom security agents on frontier models, followed by Falcon IQ and SafeMind at Fal.Con 2026 [5]. Market Share (1/2): Record net new ARR of ~$333M (+51% YoY) shows the platform is taking wallet share, but no fetched source quantified category share, so this is scored as a meaningful player rather than a documented leader [1]. Pipeline (2/2): Management guided FY2027 net new ARR to $1.350-1.359B (+34%) and exited Q2 with a record Q3 pipeline, while the Agentic Identity Provider and the $260M Pangea and $290M Onum acquisitions target AI-agent security as a named next-generation category [1][4]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2026 R&D of $1.385B equals 28.8% of revenue, top quartile for infrastructure software [3].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): CrowdStrike's 'We stop breaches' mission is specific and visibly drives product decisions, from single-agent architecture to the 2026 push into securing autonomous AI agents, though it has not yet been validated across decades [9][4]. Community Impact (1/2): The company publishes an ESG program overseen by the board and executive team, but no distinctive dollar-quantified community program surfaced in research [9]. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found after searching. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP Form 4 data shows zero open-market purchases against roughly 2,100 insider sale transactions across calendar 2026, a clear net-selling pattern [7].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Growth-sleeve calculation: D/E 16.0% scores 1.0 (1x); ROE 1.46% scores 0.10 (2x); revenue growth 25.8% scores 1.0 (1x); 5-year revenue CAGR of 40.6% (FY2021 $874M to FY2026 $4.81B, derived from reported revenue) scores 1.0 (2x); forward P/E 155.4 scores 0.0 (1x); profit margin 0.83% scores 0.04 (1x); Yahoo-reported PEG 6.74 scores 0.0 (2x) [2][3]. Weighted sum 4.24 / 10 = 4. The balance sheet is pristine ($5.01B cash vs $820M debt) and free cash flow is ~$2.0B, but stock-based compensation keeps GAAP margins near zero and the valuation far above every scoring floor [2]. Liquidity floor easily cleared at ~9.8M shares x $250 = ~$2.45B daily.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Analysts at Constellation Research argue CrowdStrike's telemetry data flywheel is a moat against AI agents and that agentic AI adds a demand tailwind, because every deployed agent becomes new attack surface requiring identity and runtime protection [6]. The residual exposure is the broader market's questioning of seat-based enterprise software in an agentic world, which Kurtz acknowledged directly, and the risk that hyperscalers bundle 'good enough' AI security [4]. AI Opportunity (1/1): The entire $5.84B ARR platform is sold as AI-native, and Charlotte AI, AgentWorks and Falcon IQ are monetized AI products shipping today [1][5].

infinite_game.summary: CrowdStrike has a genuine, concrete cause in stopping breaches and has kept building toward it through the July 2024 outage and the agentic-AI shift, which Sinek would respect. But a decade-old cause untested across leadership transitions, heavy insider selling, and competitive language aimed at displacing rivals keep it in MIXED territory rather than a proven infinite player.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'We stop breaches' is service-oriented and never fully achievable, and leadership references it when explaining moves such as securing AI agents with verifiable identities [4][9]. It remains founder-era and has not survived a leadership transition or multi-decade test, so it is a genuine cause partially lived rather than a proven competitive advantage.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): After the 2024 outage the company kept funding R&D at ~29% of revenue and spent $550M on Pangea and Onum to build AI-agent security ahead of proven demand [3][4]. These are real long-term bets, but they are also consistent with growth-at-scale playbooks rather than sacrifices of current earnings in service of the cause.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Founder-CEO George Kurtz has led since 2011 and the company continues to attract senior talent such as former NVIDIA executive Bartley Richardson as Chief AI and Autonomous Systems Officer [5]. No retention or employee-survey data was found, so the organization is scored as adequately trusting rather than exceptional.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): CrowdStrike evolved from an endpoint product into a multi-module platform and is now repositioning around agentic security operations, with Kurtz predicting the AI-agent category will outgrow core endpoint [4]. These are expansions of the core rather than abandonment of a profitable business.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Research surfaced no management commentary acknowledging competitors' strengths; messaging frames the opportunity as replacing legacy tools and consolidating spend onto Falcon, a finite displacement framing [1][4].

investment_thesis: CrowdStrike is executing a clean beat-and-raise cycle two years after its 2024 outage: fiscal Q2 2027 revenue rose 26% to $1.47B, ARR reached $5.84B, and record net new ARR of ~$333M grew 51% and beat the high end of guidance by more than $45M [1]. Management raised FY2027 net new ARR guidance to $1.350-1.359B (+34%) and revenue to $5.99-6.01B, expects at least a 30% free cash flow margin, and exited the quarter with a record pipeline [1]. The balance sheet holds $5.01B of cash against $820M of debt, and AI agents expand the attack surface CrowdStrike is built to defend, with Charlotte AI AgentWorks, Falcon IQ and the Agentic Identity Provider positioning the company for the category Kurtz expects to outgrow endpoint [2][4][5].
thesis_continued: The bear case is valuation and quality of earnings. At ~155x forward earnings and a 6.7 PEG, with a GAAP profit margin under 1% and ROE of 1.5%, the shares discount years of flawless execution, and any ARR deceleration could compress the multiple sharply [2]. Insiders have made roughly 2,100 sales and no open-market purchases in 2026 [7]. Governance overhangs include a reported DOJ/SEC inquiry into a $32M Carahsoft deal and possible 'pre-booking', even though a shareholder fraud suit over the 2024 outage was dismissed in January 2026 [8]. The Inspire Impact Score of -49 (MISALIGNED) may limit allocation for faith-based mandates.
key_catalysts: Net new ARR acceleration toward the raised FY2027 target of $1.350-1.359B (+34%), with the record Q3 pipeline converting in the December quarter report [1]
Monetization of Falcon IQ, SafeMind and Charlotte AI AgentWorks launched at RSAC and Fal.Con 2026 as enterprises deploy autonomous agents that need identity and runtime security [5]
Integration of the Pangea ($260M) and Onum ($290M) acquisitions into an AI-agent security and data pipeline offering that Kurtz expects to eventually outgrow endpoint [4]
key_risks: Multiple compression from ~155x forward P/E and 6.7 PEG if FY2027 growth slows below the ~25% revenue guide [2]
Resolution of the reported DOJ/SEC inquiry into the $32M Carahsoft transaction could bring penalties or revenue-recognition restatements [8]
Hyperscaler bundling and AI-native entrants pressuring pricing as the market questions seat-based enterprise software in an agentic world [4]
